claim: A star about 30 million light-years away
quote: The volatile star, known as AT 2016blu, is in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, located about 30 million light-years from Earth.

claim: It keeps erupting like a supernova, and surviving
quote: This star’s behavior was confusing at first because it kept acting like a supernova, but clearly it’s not because it keeps surviving these outbursts about three times a year

claim: (same)
quote: The spikes in brightness are so extreme that they resemble supernova explosions

claim: At least 27 bursts between 2012 and 2026
quote: Between 2012 and 2026, astronomers detected at least 27 bursts of optical light

claim: They call it a supernova impostor
quote: AT 2016blu is also referred to as a “supernova impostor.”

claim: Chandra caught it at least 100 times brighter in X-rays than before its outbursts began
quote: Chandra data from March 2026 revealed that AT 2016blu was at least 100 times brighter in X-rays than in Chandra data from 2001 to 2002, which is before the outbursts began.

claim: Chandra caught it during an outburst
quote: When these observations showed that the star was in outburst in early 2026, Chandra observations were triggered and obtained in March 2026

claim: The best explanation: a black hole or neutron star
quote: The best explanation for this is that material from the star is falling onto a neutron star or black hole

claim: A hidden partner pulling material off it every 113 days
quote: a previously hidden companion object that keeps pulling material away from the massive star every 113 days as they orbit one another

claim: The partner is a black hole or a neutron star
quote: This partner is either a stellar-mass black hole, or the dense collapsed core of a massive star called a neutron star.

claim: First X-ray detection of this class of erupting star
quote: This is the first X-ray detection of one of this class of erupting stars.

claim: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, Wednesday, November 18
quote: NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth

claim: NEXT card fact: one light-day is more than 16 billion miles
quote: which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers)

claim: NEXT card fact: light from Earth takes 24 hours to reach Voyager 1
quote: any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft

claim: The galaxy photo is a Chandra X-ray and SDSS optical composite of NGC 4559
quote: A composite NASA Chandra X-ray and Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) optical image of the galaxy NGC 4559

claim: The ring marks the small group of pink and blue dots near the frame center, where AT 2016blu is
quote: Sitting near the outer edge of the dense spiral, near the center of the frame, is a small group of pink and blue dots.

claim: (same)
quote: The smallest pink dot in the square is AT 2016blu

claim: Galaxy photo credit
quote: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al.; Optical: SDSS; Image Processing: NASA/CXC/SAO/P. Edmonds

claim: The four-panel image shows AT 2016blu quiet and in outburst (optical, top) and Chandra X-ray before and during (bottom)
quote: Images showing AT 2016blu in outburst and quiescence.

claim: Four-panel X-ray, before: Chandra data from 2001 and 2002 (label printed on the image: "Chandra X-ray: 2001 and 2002")
quote: Chandra X-ray data obtained in 2001 and 2002

claim: Four-panel X-ray, during: Chandra data from March 24 to 27, 2026 (label printed on the image: "Chandra X-ray: March 24-27, 2026")
quote: the bottom-right image shows Chandra data obtained between March 24 and March 27, 2026

claim: Four-panel credit
quote: X-ray: NASA/CXC/Univ. of Virgina/M. Aghakhanloo et al; Optical: NSF/KAIT

claim: The star is at least 33 times the mass of the Sun (chip)
quote: Astronomers estimate the mass of this star is at least 33 times that of the Sun.
